subject: SIG: Encryption controls — KMS/HSM topology and rotation cadence
messages:
From: Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@payflux.com
Date: Tue, 22 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM and rotation details

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the initial SIG submission. The PayFlux security team reviewed your answers and requested a few clarifications specifically around encryption and key management before we can mark the control as satisfied:

1) High-level topology: Are production data-encryption keys backed by an HSM (Cloud HSM or customer HSM) or only KMS-managed CMKs? If both, which assets use HSM-backed keys vs software/KMS keys?
2) Key material lifecycle: Do you ever export raw key material from the HSM? If not, where is key material generated and stored?
3) Rotation cadence: What is the default rotation schedule for service/tenant keys (days)? Is rotation automated and audited?
4) Envelope encryption details: Confirm algorithms and negotiated TLS versions in-transit, and the envelope scheme used at rest.
5) Audit evidence: Can you provide an excerpt of key-rotation/audit logs for the last 12 months and the HSM certificate chain for FIPS validation?

We appreciate concise answers and any artifacts (architecture diagram, rotation log excerpt, cert chain). If someone technical can be looped in, that would help.

Thanks,
Andrew
Security Engineer
PayFlux

- once Dev confirms, we will attach the rotation audit excerpt and the HSM cert chain.

High level summary from a product/security perspective (short):
- In-transit: TLS 1.3 (mutual TLS for internal control channels), strong cipher suites only.
- At-rest: Envelope encryption with AES-256-GCM for data keys; root and master keys are HSM-backed CMKs.
- Key lifecycle: Key material is generated and protected inside HSMs (CloudHSM); we do not export raw key material.
- Rotation: Service CMKs have an automated rotation policy (365 days). Tenant/customer keys can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) or Redwood-managed; we support rotation via KMS key rotation and a controlled alias-swap process.

Dev — can you add the technical detail and the log excerpt? Neha — please confirm whether the artifacts meet PayFlux evidence requirements once uploaded.

Best,
Soojin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Andrew Nguyen <andrew@payflux.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Apr 2025 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: KMS/HSM and rotation details — technical details and artifacts attached

Hi all — technical answers and artifacts below. I've attached a small rotation-audit excerpt (key_rotation_audit_excerpt_20250421.csv) and the HSM cert chain (hsm_cert_chain.pem) to the secure drive link Soojin uploaded.

Topology and key placement:
- We use an envelope encryption model across our stack. Data keys (DEKs) are AES-256-GCM, generated per object/prefix and encrypted with a Customer Master Key (CMK).
- CMKs are AWS KMS keys backed by AWS CloudHSM (FIPS 140-2 validated HSM module) in each region. For on-prem/private deployments, we support an equivalent HSM-backed KMIP-compliant appliance or allow customer-supplied HSMs via our Private deployment options.
- Some ephemeral keys used for short-lived caches are generated in-process and wrapped immediately by a CMK; master key material never leaves the HSM.

Key material lifecycle / export policy:
- We NEVER export raw key material from the HSM. All CMKs are created with origin=AWS_KMS (HSM-protected) or via imported key material for BYOK where the customer performed import into their HSM/KMS.
- For BYOK imports we store only the KMS key identifier and usage metadata; the private key material remains under the customer's control in their HSM.

Rotation policy and process:
- Redwood-managed service CMKs: automated rotation set to 365 days. Rotation is implemented by creating a new cryptographic key version in KMS, re-wrapping the DEKs, and atomically swapping aliases to minimize downtime.
- Tenant/customer-managed keys (BYOK): rotation cadence is customer-controlled; Redwood supports an alias-swap procedure and provides tooling to rewrap existing DEKs using the new key version.
- Rotation is logged to our central audit pipeline: KMS/CloudTrail events, CloudHSM audit logs, and application-level rotation events are retained in the audit store. Default retention for rotation logs is 7 years, searchable via our audit interface.
- Key rotation steps (high level):
  1) Schedule rotation window and notify stakeholders.
  2) Create new key version in KMS/CloudHSM and grant necessary key policies.
  3) Re-wrap DEKs in a rolling manner (background re-encryption) to avoid mass downtime.
  4) Swap alias to new CMK version and retire old key version following retention and legal hold processes.

Algorithms and in-transit controls:
- TLS: TLS 1.3 required for all external and internal endpoints. For internal control-plane channels we use mTLS (mutual TLS) with cert pinning between services.
- Envelope encryption: DEKs use AES-256-GCM. DEKs encrypted with RSA/EC-based KMS operations depending on KMS provider; on AWS this is KMS Encrypt/Decrypt (AES-GCM DEKs wrapped by KMS).

Auditability and evidence provided:
- We captured a CSV excerpt of KMS rotation events for the last 12 months (attached: key_rotation_audit_excerpt_20250421.csv). Fields include timestamp, key_id, operation, initiated_by, and event_id.
- HSM certificate chain attached (hsm_cert_chain.pem) showing FIPS-validated module certificate chain for our CloudHSM endpoints.
- Architecture diagram (payflux_SIG_uploaded_kms_architecture.pdf) describes multi-region CMK placement, envelope flow, and optional BYOK paths.

Limitations / notes:
- For customers on Dedicated/Private deployments where they bring their own HSM, Redwood does not have access to the private key material; evidence is limited to key operation logs and signed attestation from the customer's HSM if requested.
- If PayFlux requires a signed attestation from our HSM vendor (NLT attestation or hardware CSP report), we can coordinate via our security team — please confirm the exact artifact.

If you need a sample CloudTrail query or the specific key IDs in your region for test data, tell us which region and we will provide the minimal set.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Soojin / Dev — thanks for the quick, thorough responses and the artifacts. The diagram and the audit excerpt look good at a high level. A couple of small requests to close the control: 

- Can you attach the HSM certificate chain directly in the email (we see the drive link but need a copy in the ticket)? We need it for our FIPS proofing process.
- Please provide either (a) a salted hash of the current CMK key identifiers for our reference or (b) a short mapping of example key aliases we should expect to see in our CloudTrail-based collection (region + alias format). This will help our SIEM mapping.

If you can send those two items I can mark the SIG encryption section as satisfied and move the packet to the legal review.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Andrew
PayFlux Security Team
